a.summary: F2's EXTENSION_NAMES.length sub-gap is not closed by the new guard, and moving the name lookup onto the error paths made the missing-entry failure latent instead of immediate.
a.failure_scenario: A maintainer syncs a new upstream extension at wire ID 29: regenerates the fixture to 30 rows, bumps the two hard-coded 29s to 30, adds a record to MintTokenExtension's permits and a 'case 29 -> PermissionedTransferConfig.read(data, i)' arm, but forgets to append a 30th EXTENSION_NAMES entry. Every happy-path parse succeeds (the array is now read only on error paths), the new population guard passes (concreteTypes and fixtureTypes both hold the new class), and the build ships. In production, an on-chain Token-2022 account whose ordinal-29 TLV header declares a length that disagrees with the parsed record makes line 121 evaluate EXTENSION_NAMES[29] and throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 29 out of bounds for length 29 instead of the documented IllegalArgumentException, so any caller catching IllegalArgumentException around parseExtensions/Token2022.read does not catch it.

b.summary: F2's third assertion — pinning EXTENSION_NAMES.length against the dispatch range — was not added, and this commit added a second unguarded EXTENSION_NAMES[extensionType] index site inside requireLength while deleting the instanceof early exit; nothing in `check` forces the names table to grow with the switch.
b.failure_scenario: SPL ships extension ID 29 and a maintainer follows AGAVE_SYNC.md's sync instruction: adds `case 29 -> NewExt.read(data, i)` to Token2022.parseExtensions, adds `NewExt` to MintTokenExtension's permits clause, regenerates solana-token2022-extensions.tsv with 30 rows and bumps the two `29` row-count literals at SolanaUpstreamLayoutConformanceTests.java:118 and :556 — but does not append a 30th entry to EXTENSION_NAMES. If the new extension is variable-length (fixture columns rust_short_accepts/rust_long_accepts = "n/a", exactly as TokenMetadata's row 19 is), the `if (fixed)` block at :155-170 is skipped, no error-path assertion runs, and `check` is green. In production a mint whose extension-29 TLV declares a length the reader disagrees with reaches Token2022.java:121 and throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 29 out of bounds for length 29` instead of the documented `IllegalArgumentException("Extension NewExt claims N bytes, expected M.")`. Even for a fixed-length row the only thing that catches it is the exact-message comparison at :163-168 — `assertAcceptance` at :622-625 explicitly accepts IndexOutOfBoundsException as a valid rejection.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
